newsitem.title: PERU: Peru announces $2 billion anti-drugs campaign.
newsitem.headline: Peru announces $2 billion anti-drugs campaign.

text.p: Peru, the world's largest producer of coca leaves, the raw material for cocaine, announced a $2 billion programme to fight the drug trade on Thursday.
Health Minister Marino Costa Bauer, who heads the government's anti-drugs policies, said the plan will focus on the development of alternative crops.

"We believe that it is necessary to give cocaine-producing regions means of communication, roads and airports that are indispensable for the trade of products that can substitute cocaine production," he added.
Costa said the government would put up an initial $500 million and hoped donors would match that sum by the year 2000. Peru would seek the other $1 billion at a later date.

Peru has traditionally supplied coca leaves and paste for refining into cocaine in Colombia. But U.N. officials believe intense anti-drugs operations in Colombia are leading to growing production in of cocaine in Peru and Bolivia.
These two countries have produced the bulk of the world's coca leaves, most of which went to Colombia for processing.
Costa calculated $800 million is earned illegally every year from coca and cocaine production in Peru.
About 800,000 Peruvians live directly or indirectly off this illegal business, according to a study published by the private Lima-based Centre for the Education and Prevention of Drug Use.
